clue.text: Recruits demolished Sing Sing

indicators.note: something demolished is knocked apart, so the letters of the prison's name are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Somebody has wrecked the famous New York prison.
explanation.walkthrough: Sing Sing is a high-security prison in New York State; its eight letters are the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are nouns for people taken on by a team or firm, as when a club announces its new players.

clue.text: Feature of stern father is bottling up love

indicators.note: to bottle something up is to keep it shut inside, so the word for father holds the other piece within it

parts.note: pop is an informal word for father
love is nil in tennis scoring, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A stern dad who keeps his affection hidden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stern' looks like an adjective describing the father; it is the back end of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A poop deck is the raised deck at the rear of a sailing ship, a structure found at the stern.

clue.text: 8 in lively dance

indicators.note: in here means put in other words: the answer to clue 8 restated, with its repeated half kept doubled

parts.note: the answer to clue 8 is a word for a metal container written twice, and that container is also called a can

explanation.surface: Clue 8 doing a high-kicking dance.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-referenced answer is two tins; a tin is also a can, so restating it gives the dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The French high-kicking cabaret routine is the classic energetic stage dance of the Moulin Rouge.

clue.text: Placates wild animals, feeding them vegetables

indicators.note: the greens are fed into the animals, going inside them

parts.note: apes are animals found in the wild
peas are green vegetables

explanation.surface: Someone calms down wild creatures by giving them their greens.
explanation.definitionFit: To placate and to appease both mean to calm someone by giving them what they want; both verbs are in the third person.

clue.text: A ruling in hearing is bringing accusation

indicators.note: a hearing is listening, so the words are taken as they sound when spoken

parts.note: ruling as a monarch is reigning, giving a reigning

explanation.surface: A judge's decision at a court hearing involves a formal accusation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hearing' looks like a court session, which fits the legal surface; it is the sound signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To arraign is to call someone before a court to answer a criminal charge, so it is bringing an accusation.

clue.text: It takes the lead as French land on time

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece sits on top of the next

parts.note: terre is the French word for land

explanation.surface: Something takes charge as France sets down its land in time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes the lead' suggests leading; it is a lead or rein passing through the ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A terret is a metal ring on a harness or dog collar through which reins or a leash are passed.

clue.text: Two talk wildly about one measure for power

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the next piece
the words are treated wildly, thrown around into a new order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Two people chattering wildly about one way of measuring power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wildly' rearranges TWO TALK, and 'about' puts that around I.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of a thousand watts is a standard measure of electrical power.

clue.text: Highlight popular young hero

parts.note: a highlight in hair is a tint of colour
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: The best moment of a well-liked boy's adventures.
explanation.definitionFit: Hergé's comic-strip character is a boy reporter, the youthful hero of the Belgian adventure books.

clue.text: How rifles may be carried by soldiers not wanted in retreat

definitions.text: How rifles may be carried by soldiers

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the phrase is written in reverse

parts.note: de trop is a French phrase used in English for unwanted or superfluous

explanation.surface: Unwanted soldiers carrying rifles as they retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: De trop, French for 'too much', is used in English to mean unwelcome.
explanation.definitionFit: Port arms is a military drill position: a rifle held diagonally across the body is said to be carried that way.

clue.text: Its players react competitively after every match

definitions.text: Its players react competitively after every match

parts.words: Its players react competitively after every match
parts.note: in this children's card game, players race to call out when two cards of the same value turn up one after another

explanation.surface: Sportsmen who compete keenly after each fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' suggests a sporting fixture; it is two identical cards. It also hints at the theme: every down answer pairs each of its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The card game is won by being first to call out when a pair of matching cards appears.

clue.text: It's clear a band used awfully elaborate lighting fixtures

indicators.note: letters used awfully are badly handled, so they are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A group of musicians has clearly misused some fancy lights.
explanation.definitionFit: Branched holders for several candles or lamps are ornate fittings for providing light.

clue.text: Multinational organisation exists, working for total agreement

parts.note: the UN is the United Nations
is means exists
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: The United Nations is up and running, aiming for complete consensus.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting together with one voice is complete agreement, as in singing all on one note.

clue.text: One dreadful scene eclipses another in process of aging

indicators.note: to eclipse is to cover, so the jumbled letters surround the other piece
a dreadful scene is a mess, so its letters are put out of order

parts.note: another means a second dreadful scene, its five letters also muddled, here into the order the answer needs

explanation.surface: A terrible scene overshadows the next one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dreadful' muddles SCENE into SEN...CE, and 'eclipses' wraps that round another muddled scene, ESCEN; the adjective serves both scenes.
explanation.definitionFit: Biological aging, the gradual deterioration of cells and organisms, is the technical term senescence covers.

clue.text: Understandings seen as target, using visual aids

definitions.text: seen as target, using visual aids
definitions.meaning: a target is in the sights of a gun, aligned with the aiming devices

explanation.surface: Perceptions observed as an aim, with the help of optical devices.
explanation.definitionFit: Insights are moments of clear understanding; split in two, the phrase means lined up in a weapon's sights.

clue.text: Reason, for example, money's held back therein

indicators.note: therein means inside it, so one piece goes in the other

parts.note: say is used to introduce an example

indicators.note: held back means turned back, so the word for money runs in reverse

parts.note: tin is an old slang word for money

explanation.surface: Reason: money, for example, is kept back there.
explanation.definitionFit: Reason in the sense of a sound mind, the mental faculty one loses when going mad.

clue.text: No opponent has drink minutes before end of game

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece comes before, above, the next

parts.note: tea is a drink
mate, or checkmate, ends a game of chess

explanation.surface: A player who isn't an opponent has a cuppa shortly before the final whistle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of game' suggests a final letter; it is the checkmate that ends chess.
explanation.definitionFit: A fellow player on the same side is by definition not an opponent.

clue.text: Give a hand to musician taking a bow — no 'bravo' at first

indicators.note: no says the named letter is removed
at first says the removed letter is the one at the start

parts.note: a double-bass player uses a bow
Bravo is the NATO alphabet word for B

explanation.surface: Applaud a performer bowing to the audience, though no one shouts bravo at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking a bow' suggests acknowledging applause; it is a bow for playing strings.
explanation.definitionFit: To assist is to help, and to give someone a hand is an idiom for helping them.

clue.text: It's spotted in exotic cacti, north of a lake in South America

indicators.note: in a down answer, north of means placed above
something spotted in a place is found inside it, so the word goes inside
exotic means strange, so the letters of the plant name are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something seen among unusual cacti, north of a South American lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exotic' rearranges the plant name and 'spotted in' places IT inside; 'north of' puts A beneath, since this is a down answer. 'It's' reads as a link at first.
explanation.definitionFit: The high-altitude lake on the Peru-Bolivia border is South America's largest freshwater lake.

clue.text: What's used to pay twice for dental coverage?

indicators.note: twice says the piece is written two times

parts.note: to pay a ship's seams is to coat them with tar, an old nautical sense of the verb

explanation.surface: What do you pay twice to cover dental work?
explanation.walkthrough: 'pay' looks like spending money; it is the old verb for sealing a ship with pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Tartar is the hard deposit that forms a coating over teeth, hence a playful dental covering.

clue.text: Capital family possesses invested in South Africa

parts.note: kin are family

indicators.note: money invested in something is put into it, so this piece goes inside

parts.note: has means possesses

explanation.surface: Family wealth put into South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like money, matching 'invested'; it is a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinshasa is the capital city of the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

clue.text: One name of prophet, as I repeatedly recollected

indicators.note: re-collected, gathered up again into a new order
repeatedly says the words are used more than once, here two times

explanation.surface: As I keep recalling, here is one of the prophet's names.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recollected' looks like remembering; read as re-collected, it rearranges two copies of AS I.
explanation.definitionFit: The Douay Bible and older texts use this Greek-derived form for Isaiah, the Old Testament prophet.

clue.text: May, in past, by taking British out, showing strength

parts.note: might is the past tense of the verb may

indicators.note: taking signals the next letter is removed
out completes the instruction that a letter leaves

explanation.surface: Theresa May, in the past, taking Britain out of Europe, showed strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May' looks like the Prime Minister; it is the verb, whose past tense is MIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Mighty describes something powerful, so it means showing great strength.

clue.text: Damage sign in grass

parts.note: to mar is to damage
the Ram, Aries, is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Damage a sign stuck in the grass.
explanation.definitionFit: Marram is a coarse grass planted on sand dunes to bind them together.

clue.text: It monitors movement of liquid resources we had over one period and most of another

definitions.text: It monitors movement of liquid resources

indicators.note: to have someone over is to hold them in your home, so the first word goes around the next pieces

parts.note: one is A
a term is a period, as at school

indicators.note: most of a word is all but its last letter

parts.note: another means another period, a second term

explanation.surface: A gauge for a resource we've used across one period and much of the next.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had over' means hosted, as a guest is had over, so the pronoun contains the rest; 'most of' drops a final letter. 'resources' completes the definition: water is a supplied resource.
explanation.definitionFit: A domestic meter measures the flow of supplied water into a building, so it tracks the liquid used.

clue.text: King and queen, perhaps, reversed course of action

indicators.note: reversed says the pieces are written back to front

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
a queen is a female cat, hence perhaps

explanation.surface: Two chess or card royals turned back by a change of plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'queen' suggests royalty beside 'King'; a queen is a female cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A tack is a line of approach, as in sailing, so it means a chosen way of proceeding.

clue.text: Express disapproval over what splits TV dancer's costume

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece sits over the next

parts.note: tut is the clicking sound of disapproval
U comes between T and V in the alphabet

explanation.surface: Tut-tutting at a TV dancer's skimpy outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'TV' looks like television; U is the letter splitting T and V in the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutu is the stiff short skirt worn by a ballerina.

clue.text: Narrow window for research publication

definitions.meaning: a tall narrow pointed window in Gothic architecture
A leading British medical journal publishing research

explanation.surface: A slim window opening for releasing findings.
explanation.definitionFit: Lancet is both the slim pointed arch window and the name of the famous medical journal.

clue.text: Again connect the cart and a convertible thus

indicators.note: something convertible can be changed in form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Hook the cart back up to a convertible car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'convertible' looks like a car; it signals that THE CART and A are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To reattach is to fasten something back on, connecting it once more.
